title: Route default-chat client tool completions by session URI
body:
Fix #323305

Client-provided tool calls running in a session's default chat were being silently dropped: the SDK handler's deferred never resolved, so the agent could hang waiting on a tool result that already came back.

## Why

`ChatToolCallComplete` envelopes are emitted on the chat channel URI, which is formatted as `ahp-chat://<chatId>/<base64(sessionUri)>`. Both call sites in `agentSideEffects.ts` forwarded that chat URI straight to `agent.onClientToolCallComplete(...)`. But every agent keys its `_sessions` map by the raw session id, resolved via `AgentSession.id(uri)` = `uri.path.substring(1)`. For a chat URI the path is the base64 blob, not the session GUID, so the default-chat lookup never matched and the completion was discarded.

## Fix

Forward the resolved session URI (`sessionChannel`, which both sites already computed) for the default chat so `AgentSession.id` yields the GUID. Peer (non-default) chats are tracked separately in `_chatSessions` keyed by the chat URI, so those keep being forwarded as-is via `isDefaultChatUri` check.

This is a call-site translation only; the agent `onClientToolCallComplete` implementations are unchanged. It fixes the copilot, claude, and codex agents at once.

## Note

I could not run the type-checker or tests in this worktree because `node_modules` is not installed. The change is small, reuses the already-imported `isDefaultChatUri` helper and in-scope `sessionChannel`, and the pre-commit hygiene hook passed.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Fix markdown preview scrolling editor to wrong position on click
body:
Fixes #323245

## What this PR does

When a `.md` file is open in split view with the preview, clicking back
into the editor after scrolling the preview causes the editor to jump to
a completely unrelated scroll position. Text between the previous cursor
position and the click target is also spuriously selected.

## Root cause

The `scrollEditorWithPreview` feature works by having the preview
webview post a `revealLine` message on every scroll event. A
`scrollDisabledCount` guard in the webview is supposed to suppress
scroll events that result from programmatic scrolls (to prevent feedback
loops). However the guard had two problems:

1. **Webview side (`preview-src/index.ts`):** When
   `onDidChangeTextEditorSelection` fires, the preview calls
   `scrollToRevealSourceLine` inside `doAfterImagesLoaded` — an async
   Promise. The existing guard timers (50ms) expire before
   `window.scrollTo` actually fires because the async image-load delay
   pushes the scroll past the guard window. The resulting scroll DOM
   event is not suppressed, so a stale `revealLine` message is posted to
   the extension host, which calls `editor.revealLine` at the wrong
   position.

2. **Extension host side (`src/preview/preview.ts`):** There was no
   guard in `onDidScrollPreview` to detect that an incoming `revealLine`
   message originated from an editor selection change rather than a
   genuine user scroll of the preview.

## Changes

**`preview-src/index.ts`** — In the `onDidChangeTextEditorSelection`
message handler, increment `scrollDisabledCount` with a 300ms guard
window. This covers the full async path of `doAfterImagesLoaded` +
`window.scrollTo` + one event loop tick. The counter is decremented
using `Math.max(0, count - 1)` to prevent it going negative if timers
race.

**`src/preview/preview.ts`** — Add a `#isSyncingFromEditorSelection`
flag that is set for 400ms whenever `onDidChangeTextEditorSelection`
fires (called via the new `notifyEditorSelectionChanged()` method before
the message is posted). In `onDidScrollPreview`, return early when this
flag is active. This is a defensive second layer in case a scroll
message leaks through the webview-side guard due to platform timing
differences. `clearTimeout(#editorSelectionSyncTimer)` is added to
`dispose()` to prevent timer leaks.

## How to test

1. Open any `.md` file with enough content to scroll (150+ lines).
2. Press `Ctrl+K V` to open the preview in split view.
3. Click into the preview pane.
4. Scroll the preview down to a distant section (e.g. line 100+).
5. Click back into the editor at a position near the top (e.g. line 5).

**Before this fix:** the editor jumps to the position the preview just
scrolled to, and text from the original cursor position to the click
target is selected.

**After this fix:** the cursor lands cleanly at the clicked position
with no spurious scroll or selection.

title: git: allow direct editing of staged files in diff editor
body:
Fixes #263110

  ## What this PR does

  Allows users to directly type and edit the content of staged files in the diff editor (right/modified side), and save changes back
  to the git index with Ctrl+S.

  Previously, the right side of the staged file diff editor was always read-only because:
  1. The git:// file system provider was registered with `isReadonly: true` (provider-level readonly)
  2. `stat()` returned `FilePermission.Readonly` for `ref=''` (the index direct reference used on the staged diff right side)
  3. `textFileService.save()` had no path for custom-scheme URIs without a `TextFileEditorModel`

  ## Changes

  - **`extensions/git/src/fileSystemProvider.ts`**: Register with `isReadonly: false` and allow `stat()`/`writeFile()` for `ref=''`.
  Fire a file change event for the index URI after writes so the editor reloads with the latest index content.
  - **`extensions/git/src/repository.ts`**: Add `stageRaw(resource, data: Uint8Array)` to write raw bytes directly to the git index
  via `git hash-object --stdin -w` + `git update-index --cacheinfo`.
  - **`src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/textDiffEditor.ts`**: Derive the modified-side readonly state from `fileService.stat()`
  instead of the model's hardcoded `isReadonly()`. Cache `originalEditable` from the model to prevent the original (HEAD) side from
  becoming editable.
  - **`src/vs/workbench/services/textfile/browser/textFileService.ts`**: Add a fallback save path for custom-scheme URIs that have a
  file provider but no `TextFileEditorModel`, so Ctrl+S correctly triggers a write through the provider.

  ## How to test

  1. Open a repository with staged changes (`git add` some edits)
  2. In the Source Control panel, click a file under **Staged Changes** to open the diff editor
  3. Click into the right (modified) side — it should be editable (no "Read-only" indicator)
  4. Make edits and press **Ctrl+S**
  5. Verify the change is reflected in the index: `git diff --cached`

title: AgentHost - nicer display messages for the feedback comment tools
body:
## What

The agent host's feedback "comment" server tools — `addComment`, `listComments`, `deleteComments`, `resolveComments`, `viewUnreviewedComments` — had no display handling, so they fell through to the generic `Using/Used "<toolName>"` fallback (and `Calling/Called listComments` on Codex). This gives them real invocation/past-tense messages across **all three** agent harnesses, e.g. "Checking comments" → "Checked 3 comments".

## How

These are provider-agnostic **server** tools (one `feedbackServerToolGroup`, executed against the annotations channel and advertised on `SessionState.serverTools`), but their display was being authored per-provider — so a first pass that only touched Copilot would still leave Claude showing `Used "listComments"` and Codex showing `Called listComments`.

Instead of triplicating, the display is hoisted into the group that owns the tools:

- **`IServerToolGroup`** gains an optional `getDisplay(toolName, args, result?)` returning `{ displayName?, invocationMessage?, pastTenseMessage? }`. The host module stays feature-agnostic.
- **`feedbackServerToolGroup`** implements it once, including the `listComments` "Checked N comments" count parsed from the tool result.
- A new pure **`getServerToolDisplay`** dispatcher (`serverToolGroups.ts`, now the single source of truth wired into `AgentServerToolHost`) matches a tool by bare name **or** transport-prefixed form (Claude's `mcp__host__<name>`), so it works on the providers' history-replay paths too.
- Copilot, Claude, and Codex display layers consult the dispatcher first and fall back to their existing generic message otherwise.

## Tests

- New `serverToolGroups.test.ts` covers all 5 tools, the count plural/singular/missing/malformed cases, the `mcp__host__listComments` prefix match, and unknown → `undefined`.
- `copilotToolDisplay.test.ts` keeps a delegation smoke check; exhaustive cases moved to the shared test.
- Full node unit suite: 11640 passing, 0 failing.

(Written by Copilot)

title: fix: defer model disposal until after input state flush when switching chat threads (#309115)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #309115

**Bug:** Chat input prompt text was not saved when switching between threads, causing the user's in-progress prompt to be lost.

**Root Cause:** In `ChatViewPane.showModel()`, the old model reference was disposed immediately via `this.modelRef.value = undefined`, which triggered model serialization before the widget's `setModel` call could flush the current input state to the outgoing model.

**Fix:** Use `clearAndLeak()` to extract the old reference without disposing it, then manually dispose it after `setModel` has been called (which triggers the input state flush). Early-return and error paths also properly dispose the old reference to prevent leaks.

## Changes

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widgetHosts/viewPane/chatViewPane.ts`: Replace immediate `this.modelRef.value = undefined` with `clearAndLeak()` pattern that defers disposal until after `setModel` flushes input state. Added proper disposal in all early-return and error paths.
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/model/chatModelStore.test.ts`: Added 2 regression tests validating the disposal ordering behavior for issue #309115.

## Testing

- Added regression test verifying model stays alive when reference is leaked and disposed after state flush
- Added regression test demonstrating the problematic early-release pattern that caused the bug
- All existing tests pass

perf: fix expensive git commands in GVFS repos (chat sessions)
body:
The VS Code Copilot chat sessions extension triggers expensive git commands that are problematic in GVFS (VFSForGit) repos:

1. **`git add -A -- .`** with a temp index scans the entire directory tree, hydrating all placeholder directories in GVFS repos (>10min on large repos -> ~0.5s with this fix)
2. **Temp-index git commands** (`read-tree`, `add`, `write-tree`, `diff --cached`) don't set `COMMAND_HOOK_LOCK`, so the GVFS command hook holds the main lock and blocks file writes
3. **Rename detection** in diff commands downloads blob content for similarity analysis -- extremely expensive in GVFS

## Changes

### Unconditional (safe on all repos):

**Targeted file staging** -- Replace `git add -A -- .` with `--pathspec-from-file` using the git extension's already-computed change list. Only modified files are staged, avoiding full directory tree scans.

**COMMAND_HOOK_LOCK** -- Set on all `exec()` calls that use `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. Prevents the GVFS command hook from holding the main lock during temp-index operations. Ignored on non-GVFS repos.

### GVFS-only (gated on `core.virtualfilesystem`):

**`--no-renames`** -- Added to diff commands when GVFS is detected. Renames appear as delete+add pairs instead.

## Files changed

- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/git/vscode-node/utils.ts` -- New helpers: `buildTempIndexEnv`, `getChangedFilePaths`, `stageChangedFiles`, `isGvfsRepository`
- `chatSessionWorkspaceFolderServiceImpl.ts` -- All three changes applied
- `chatSessionWorktreeServiceImpl.ts` -- All three changes applied
- `chatSessionWorktreeCheckpointServiceImpl.ts` -- Targeted staging + COMMAND_HOOK_LOCK. Also changed `read-tree` to always use HEAD.

## Open questions for reviewers

- **`--numstat` kept**: Main cost driver (255s vs 5s) but `statistics` field is consumed by UI. Could be made lazy in follow-up.

## :warning: Draft status

Not build-tested. Submitted as a draft to propose the approach.

Cache Middleware ignores Vary: Authorization / Vary: Cookie leading to cross-user cache leakage

CSS Declaration Injection via Style Object Values in JSX SSR

Affects: hono/utils/jwt. Fixes improper validation of exp, nbf, and iat claims, where falsy, non-finite, or non-numeric values could silently bypass time-based checks instead of being rejected per RFC 7519. GHSA-hm8q-7f3q-5f36

title: nes(xtab): detect duplicate additions in diff-patch + adversarial-review fixes
body:
Builds the diff-patch-response duplicate-additions heuristic and applies the fixes from the adversarial review of that work, in two commits:

## Commit 1 — `nes(xtab): detect & strip duplicate additions in diff-patch response`

The diff-patch model can occasionally emit additions that copy the lines immediately following the deleted range, which would produce visibly duplicated code (e.g. an extra closing brace). Adds a heuristic that detects three duplication shapes and trims them, gated behind a new team-internal experiment-based setting (default off).

- New helper `tryRemoveDuplicateAdditions` recognizes **suffix**, **prefix**, and **middle** duplications. Only one shape is applied per patch.
- A "meaningful line" guard (`line.trim().length > 1`) protects single-token insertions like `}` / `;` / `)` from being dropped as false positives in the prefix/middle cases.
- `XtabCustomDiffPatchResponseHandler.handleResponse` takes a new flag controlling dedup behavior.

## Commit 2 — `nes(xtab): apply adversarial review fixes to dedup heuristic`

Five fixes from an adversarial review of commit 1:

1. **Headline-bug false negative fixed.** A pure-additive single-`}` patch (`addedLines = ['}']`, `removedLines = []`) duplicating the next line's `}` was previously preserved by an over-zealous "all-non-meaningful suffix" guard. The guard is removed: applying such a patch would insert a stray closing token into already-balanced code, which is precisely the case the dedup was meant to fix. Trade-off: a rare false positive in mid-typing unbalanced files; we optimize for the common balanced case.

2. **Middle-shape collateral fixed.** The previous middle case dropped everything from the matched pair to the end of `addedLines`, even content that wasn't verified as duplicate. Replaced with a greedy extension that drops only the verified-equal range; trailing new content is preserved.

3. **`'off' | 'log' | 'remove'` mode.** The boolean `removeDuplicateAdditions` setting becomes a `DuplicateAdditionsMode` enum so we can ship a measurement phase first to learn the heuristic's firing rate before flipping user-visible behavior. Setting renamed to `chat.advanced.inlineEdits.xtabProvider.diffPatch.duplicateAdditionsMode`.

4. **Operate on canonical types.** `tryRemoveDuplicateAdditions` now takes `LineReplacement` + `AbstractText` instead of raw tuples, matching the surrounding edit-pipeline conventions. The handler builds the `LineReplacement` once and yields a fresh one after trimming — no more in-place mutation of `Patch.addedLines`.

5. **Return `NoSuggestions` even when all patches are dropped.** The prior `FilteredOut("diffPatch:duplicateAdditions:N")` branch bypassed the cache (causing re-fetch) and the cursor-jump retry. The handler now always returns `NoSuggestions` and exposes a per-event `onDuplicateRemoved` callback so callers can wire telemetry without dragging `ITelemetryService` into the parser.

## Deferred follow-ups

- Relocate the dedup as a peer to `IgnoreWhitespaceOnlyChanges` in `streamEditsWithFiltering` (recommendation 4(b) of the review). The function-signature change in this PR captures most of the architectural win; the pipeline relocation is a larger change crossing the parser/filter boundary.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-check-ts-native` (extensions/copilot tsconfig) — clean
- `vitest run xtabCustomDiffPatchResponseHandler.spec.ts` — **35/35 pass** including new tests for the headline-bug fix, the greedy-middle behavior, Log/Remove/Off modes, and the `NoSuggestions`-with-callback contract
- Pre-commit hygiene check passed

The setting defaults to `off`. No user-visible behavior change ships from this PR alone.

* nes(xtab): replace single Remove mode with three duplicate-handling strategies

Previously `DuplicateAdditionsMode` had a single action mode (`Remove`)
that trimmed the duplicate portion from the patch's additions. Real-world
duplicates fall into different risk  sometimes we want toprofiles
surgically trim, sometimes the safer move is to drop the patch outright,
and sometimes a duplicate inside the stream is a signal that the whole
response has gone off the rails.

Split `Remove` into three explicit strategies, all gated by the same
team-internal setting:

- `DropPatch`: discard just the offending patch and continue processing
  the rest of the stream. Use when individual bad patches should be
  suppressed but the rest of the model's output is trustworthy.
- `DropAllRemaining`: discard the offending patch AND every subsequent
  patch from the same response. Patches already yielded before the
  detection are kept. Use when an in-stream duplicate is a kill-switch
  signal.
- `TrimDuplicate`: surgically trim just the duplicated lines from the
  patch's additions (the previous `Remove` behavior). If the trim
  leaves a no-op patch, drop it.

`Off` and `Log` are unchanged. The redacted `OnDuplicateRemovedCallback`
still fires for every action mode.

Tests: 35 pre-existing tests remain green (the `Remove`-mode cases
became `TrimDuplicate`); added 2 new tests covering the `DropPatch` and
`DropAllRemaining` semantics, including 'subsequent patches yielded
before the detection are preserved'.

title: fix: filter images from telemetry render to prevent supportsVision crash (fixes #315729)
body:
### Summary

The `sendInvokedToolTelemetry` function in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/panel/toolCalling.tsx` renders tool results asynchronously (fire-and-forget) to count tokens. When a tool result contains image data, `PrimitiveToolResult.onImage()` accesses `this.endpoint.supportsVision`, but `this.endpoint` (injected via `@IPromptEndpoint`) can be `undefined` because the parent PromptRenderer's DI tree is disposed after the parent render completes — before the fire-and-forget telemetry render finishes. This causes `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'supportsVision')` with 379K hits affecting 33K users on extension version 0.47.0.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#315729
Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312`

### How the Fix Works

**Approach** (per reviewer feedback): Make `@IPromptEndpoint` and `@IAuthenticationService` optional in `PrimitiveToolResult`'s constructor. The class should not expect these DI services to always be available — particularly during fire-and-forget telemetry renders where the parent DI tree may already be disposed. All usages now use optional chaining (`?.`) to gracefully handle the undefined case.

| `extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/panel/toolCalling.tsx` | crash site + fix location | L738-739: made DI optional; L783, L792, L823, L826, L959: added optional chaining |

## What

Bumps `@vscode/gulp-electron` from `1.41.2` to `1.41.3`.

## Why

`1.41.3` brings in microsoft/vscode-gulp-electron#42 which adds retry-with-backoff around the three network operations involved in downloading Electron (the `got` HEAD on the release asset, `getDownloadUrl`, and `@electron/get`'s `downloadArtifact`).

This fixes build breaks caused by transient DNS/network blips like:

```
[15:29:24] 'vscode-win32-x64-min-ci' errored after 17 s
[15:29:24] RequestError: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND release-assets.githubusercontent.com
```

Observed on Insider build [437760](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=437760), and likely the cause of similar one-off Windows build failures over the past months.

title: Experiment with terminal output deltas for repeated polls
body:
This adds an experimental `chat.tools.terminal.outputDeltas` setting for repeated `get_terminal_output` polling.

When the experiment is enabled:
- The first poll for a terminal execution returns the full output, preserving current context.
- Repeated polls with identical output return a short unchanged marker instead of replaying the full terminal buffer.
- Polls with appended output return only the new suffix.
- Non-prefix changes, such as screen rewrites or truncated scrollback, fall back to returning the current full output.

This change is stateful across explicit `get_terminal_output` calls and targets prompt/tool-result replay from terminal polling loops.

title: fix: guard against non-changeable extension enablement in chat setup (fixes #315293)
body:
## 🔧 Error Fix

### Summary

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Error | `unhandlederror — Cannot change enablement of GitHub Copilot Chat extension because of its extension kind` |
| Bucket ID | `7aab7d75-224e-85c0-0f1c-610ee95490ae` |
| Commit | `8b640eef` |
| Version | 1.119.0 |
| Hits / Users | 3,307 / 1,149 |
| Platforms | Windows, Mac, Linux |

The `ChatTeardownContribution.maybeEnableOrDisableExtension()` method calls `extensionsWorkbenchService.setEnablement()` on the Copilot Chat extension without first checking whether the extension's enablement state can actually be changed. When the extension is in a non-changeable state (e.g., `DisabledByExtensionKind`, `DisabledByEnvironment`, etc.), `setEnablement` throws an error that bubbles up as an unhandled error reaching telemetry.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#315293
Recommended reviewer: `@sandy081`

### Culprit Commit

This is a pre-existing issue in `chatSetupContributions.ts` — the `maybeEnableOrDisableExtension` method has never guarded against non-changeable enablement states. The error is triggered on all platforms when the Copilot Chat extension's kind prevents enablement changes (e.g., running in a remote workspace where the extension kind doesn't match).

### Code Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant ChatTeardown as ChatTeardownContribution
    participant ExtWorkbench as ExtensionsWorkbenchService
    participant ExtEnablement as ExtensionEnablementService

    ChatTeardown->>ExtWorkbench: setEnablement([copilotChat], state)
    ExtWorkbench->>ExtEnablement: setEnablement(extensions, state)
    ExtEnablement->>ExtEnablement: throwErrorIfCannotChangeEnablement(ext)
    ExtEnablement->>ExtEnablement: throwErrorIfEnablementStateCannotBeChanged(ext, state)
    Note right of ExtEnablement: EnablementState is DisabledByExtensionKind
    ExtEnablement-->>ExtWorkbench: throws Error("Cannot change enablement...")
    ExtWorkbench-->>ChatTeardown: unhandled error reaches telemetry
```

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatSetup/chatSetupContributions.ts` — `maybeEnableOrDisableExtension()`
- `src/vs/workbench/services/extensionManagement/browser/extensionEnablementService.ts` — `throwErrorIfEnablementStateCannotBeChanged()` (crash site, not modified)

### Repro Steps

1. Open VS Code in a configuration where the Copilot Chat extension's kind prevents it from running (e.g., a remote workspace where the extension kind doesn't match)
2. Trigger AI feature enable/disable flow (e.g., toggle AI features setting)
3. `maybeEnableOrDisableExtension` is called, which calls `setEnablement` without checking `canChangeEnablement`
4. The enablement service throws because the extension is `DisabledByExtensionKind`

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatSetup/chatSetupContributions.ts:786`): Added a guard clause that checks `extensionEnablementService.canChangeEnablement(defaultChatExtension.local)` before calling `setEnablement`. If the extension's enablement cannot be changed, the method returns early instead of throwing. This follows the principle of fixing at the data producer — the caller (`maybeEnableOrDisableExtension`) should verify preconditions before invoking an operation that throws on invalid state, rather than catching the error downstream.

The `canChangeEnablement` method already exists on the injected `IWorkbenchExtensionEnablementService` and wraps the same `throwErrorIfCannotChangeEnablement` check in a try/catch, returning a boolean. This is the idiomatic pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.

### Recommended Owner

`@sandy081` — owns `extensionEnablementService.ts` and `chatSetupContributions.ts`, and authored the most recent significant changes to the chat teardown contribution.

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Cache Middleware ignores Vary: Authorization / Vary: Cookie leading to cross-user cache leakage

Affects: Cache Middleware. Fixes missing cache-skip handling for Vary: Authorization and Vary: Cookie, where a response cached for one authenticated user could be served to other users. GHSA-p77w-8qqv-26rm

Affects: hono/jsx. Fixes a missing CSS-context escape for style object values and property names, where untrusted input could inject additional CSS declarations. The impact is limited to CSS and does not allow JavaScript execution. GHSA-qp7p-654g-cw7p

Affects: hono/utils/jwt. Fixes improper validation of exp, nbf, and iat claims, where falsy, non-finite, or non-numeric values could silently bypass time-based checks instead of being rejected per RFC 7519. GHSA-hm8q-7f3q-5f36

title: fix: ensure URI path starts with slash when splitting terminal with authority (fixes #316035)
body:
## 🔧 Error Fix

### Summary

**Error**: `[UriError]: If a URI contains an authority component, then the path component must either be empty or begin with a slash ("/") character`

**Bucket**: `9cce252a-6fc0-eec2-3349-14180ca8c4fd` — 1,423 hits / 939 users on version 1.119.0

**Root cause**: In `TerminalService._splitTerminal()`, when splitting a terminal whose parent has a remote authority (e.g., SSH, WSL), the child terminal's `cwd` is a plain string (e.g., a Windows path like `C:\Users\foo`). This string was passed directly as the `path` component to `URI.from()` along with the parent's authority. RFC 3986 requires that when an authority is present, the path must either be empty or start with `/`. The validation in `uri.ts:40` correctly rejects this invalid combination.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#316035
Recommended reviewer: `@Tyriar`

### Culprit Commit

This is a **pre-existing bug** in `_splitTerminal` that has been present since the split-terminal URI construction logic was introduced. It surfaces primarily in remote scenarios (SSH, WSL) where the parent terminal has an authority component and the child's cwd is a platform-native path string. Not a recent regression in the traditional sense — the spike correlates with increased remote terminal usage in 1.119.0.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[createTerminal] -->|options.location is split| B[_splitTerminal]
    B --> C{shellLaunchConfig.cwd is string?}
    C -->|yes, parent.cwd is URI| D[URI.from with parent authority + string path]
    D --> E[_validateUri]
    E -->|path doesn't start with /| F[UriError thrown]
```

### Affected Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalService.ts` | Data producer: constructs URI with invalid path |
| `src/vs/base/common/uri.ts` | Crash site: validates URI components (not modified) |

### Repro Steps

1. Connect to a remote host (SSH or WSL) so the terminal has an authority component in its cwd URI
2. Open a terminal in the remote workspace
3. Split the terminal (Ctrl+Shift+5 or the split button)
4. If the child terminal's cwd resolves to a platform-native path string (e.g., Windows path without leading `/`), the UriError is thrown

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalService.ts:1208`):

Extract the path into a local variable before passing it to `URI.from()`. When the parent's authority is non-empty and the resolved path doesn't start with `/`, prepend `/` to make it RFC 3986-compliant. This fixes at the data producer (where the URI components are assembled), not at the crash site (the URI validator). The URI validator is correct — it's the caller that was producing an invalid path component.

This is the standard pattern used throughout VS Code for converting platform paths to URI paths (e.g., Windows paths like `C:\foo` become `/C:\foo` in URI path components, as seen in `URI.file()`).

### Recommended Owner

`@Tyriar` — primary maintainer of the terminal service (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/`)

title: Prevent alt-buffer hang in agent host terminals
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/314889
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/314189

- Add Agent Host detection for commands that enter xterm's alternate screen buffer.
- Return a structured `alternateBuffer` result when a shell command opens an interactive terminal UI such as `vim`.
- Keep that shell marked busy after the tool result returns, until the command finishes or the terminal exits.
- Prevent follow-up shell commands from being routed into the existing TUI buffer, for example `echo AFTER_VIM` being typed into Vim instead of a shell.
- Keep SDK-facing tool results separate from Agent Host shell lifecycle metadata via an internal shell execution result shape.
- Cover both shell-integration and sentinel fallback execution paths.


Expected with this PR:

- The first command returns with an `alternateBuffer` style result while Vim remains open.
- `SHOULD_NOT_REACH` is not printed.
- `echo AFTER_VIM` is not typed into the existing Vim buffer; Agent Host keeps that shell busy and uses another shell for unrelated commands.



Steps to manually validate:

A repro close to the original issue is a merge commit that opens Vim for the commit message, followed by another shell command:

```sh
tmp=$(mktemp -d); cd "$tmp" && git init -q && git config user.email a@b.c && git config user.name A && echo base > f && git add f && git commit -m base -q && git checkout -q -b feature && echo feature > feature.txt && git add feature.txt && git commit -m feature -q && git checkout -q - && echo main > main.txt && git add main.txt && git commit -m main -q && git merge --no-ff --no-commit feature -q && git status --short && if [[ -f .git/MERGE_HEAD || -f $(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD) ]]; then TERM=xterm-256color GIT_EDITOR='vim -Nu NONE -n' git commit; fi && echo SHOULD_NOT_REACH
```

Then ask for:

```sh
echo AFTER_VIM
```



Follow-up:

- This follows the workbench execute-strategy signal: xterm alternate-buffer entry means the command likely launched an interactive terminal UI.
- Agent Host only implements the minimal handling for now: return `alternateBuffer`, keep the command running, and prevent the shell from being reused by unrelated tool calls.
- This can return before a command would have naturally completed if the command only enters the alternate buffer temporarily.
- Agent Host does not yet have the full workbench terminal tool flow around this signal, such as active terminal execution IDs, output monitoring, input-needed detection, idle-silence promotion, or richer follow-up terminal tools.
- Future work should bring more of that workbench flow to Agent Host for better parity.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Alternate-buffer detection comes from [`createAltBufferPromise`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d188e2d1096bc4c9251c5d293d013e12e44ffc48/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/strategyHelpers.ts#L54-L78), which checks whether xterm's active buffer is the alternate buffer and completes when that state is reached.
- Racing command completion against alternate-buffer entry comes from [`richExecuteStrategy`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d188e2d1096bc4c9251c5d293d013e12e44ffc48/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/richExecuteStrategy.ts#L160-L195) and [`basicExecuteStrategy`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d188e2d1096bc4c9251c5d293d013e12e44ffc48/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/basicExecuteStrategy.ts#L176-L240).
- The local `IShellExecutionResult` shape follows the same separation as [`ITerminalExecuteStrategyResult`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d188e2d1096bc4c9251c5d293d013e12e44ffc48/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/executeStrategy.ts#L31-L37): command execution returns terminal-specific metadata first, and the outer tool layer maps that into the final tool result.
- The `alternateBuffer` result shape and user-facing intent come from [`RunInTerminalTool`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d188e2d1096bc4c9251c5d293d013e12e44ffc48/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/runInTerminalTool.ts#L468-L469) and its `didEnterAltBuffer` handling in [`RunInTerminalTool`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d188e2d1096bc4c9251c5d293d013e12e44ffc48/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/runInTerminalTool.ts#L1758-L1768).
- The shell hold/release bookkeeping is Agent Host-specific: workbench has richer terminal execution ownership, while Agent Host has a reusable shell pool and needs to keep an early-returned alt-buffer/background shell unavailable until command finish or terminal exit.

title: Agents web: hide harness picker and host suffix in web when single harness
body:
## What

In the agents workbench (vscode.dev/agents) the new-chat empty state currently shows:

> New session in **<repo>** with **Copilot CLI [<Host>]**

This is redundant because:
- The host is **already** scoped via the host filter in the title bar — repeating it in the harness label adds noise.
- When the connected agent host advertises only a single agent (today: just `copilotcli`), the harness picker has nothing to pick. Surfacing it just invites a click that opens an empty popover.

This PR hides both, **scoped to web only**. Desktop behavior is unchanged.

## How

Two small changes:

1. **`SessionTypePicker._updateTriggerLabel`** — also adds the `.hidden` class to the trigger when `isWeb && allProviderSessionTypes.length <= 1`. The existing CSS rule on `.session-workspace-picker-with-label`:
   ```css
   .session-workspace-picker-with-label:has(+ .sessions-chat-session-type-picker .action-label.hidden) {
       display: none;
   }
   ```
   collapses the dangling "with" connector automatically — no JS coordination required.

2. **`RemoteAgentHostSessionsProvider._formatSessionTypeLabel`** — returns the bare agent label in web (`isWebPlatform`), instead of `` `${agentLabel} [${this.label}]` ``. So labels read "Copilot CLI" instead of "Copilot CLI [My Host]".

## Result

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Web, 1 harness | New session in <repo> with Copilot CLI [<Host>] | New session in <repo> |
| Web, 2+ harnesses | New session in <repo> with Copilot CLI [<Host>] (▾) | New session in <repo> with Copilot CLI (▾) |
| Desktop | (unchanged) | (unchanged) |

## Notes

- Existing tests assert the `[My Host]` suffix; they run in node so `isWeb` is `false` and they continue to pass.
- The picker hide path uses an existing class hook + CSS `:has()` rule, so no new selectors or layout work was needed.

title: fix: enable copilot-local ESLint rules in PR CI
body:
🤖 AI Assisted PR

## Problem

The Copilot ESLint plugin (`.eslintplugin/`) has two bugs that prevent `copilot-local/*` rules from running in PR CI:

**Bug 1 — Plugin fails to load.** `index.ts` uses `import * as glob from 'glob'` + `glob.sync()`. In the root ESLint's ESM context, the namespace import on CJS `glob` v5 gives `{ default: [function] }` — no `sync` property. The plugin silently fails to load, registering zero rules.

**Bug 2 — Rule checks absolute paths.** `no-unlayered-files.ts` splits `context.filename` (an absolute path) and checks if ANY segment matches a layer name. Since `vscode` is both a valid layer name AND the repo checkout directory, every file's path matches → the rule never fires.

## Impact

Since the root ESLint integration was added on April 28 (`371c4a0a73c`), **no `copilot-local/*` rules have executed in PR CI**. This includes `no-unlayered-files`, `no-test-imports`, `no-runtime-import`, and 8+ other custom rules.

On May 7, PR #314783 added a test file to the wrong folder. PR CI passed (copilot rules were dead). The ADO build caught it post-merge, causing **6 consecutive build failures** across all platforms (~55 cascading task failures, 2-hour recovery window).

**Data:** `Download Copilot VSIX` is the #1 root-cause task in the 14-day OData dataset (81 of 479 root-cause failures). 68% of those were caused by Copilot Lint failures that escaped PR CI.

## Fix

Two changes in `extensions/copilot/.eslintplugin/`:

### 1. `index.ts` — Replace `glob.sync` with `fs.readdirSync`
The `glob` package (v5, CJS) doesn't export `sync` as an ESM named export. `fs.readdirSync` is a Node.js built-in — zero external dependency, works in both CJS and ESM.

title: CI: kill lingering Windows smoke-test processes before Publish Log Files
body:
## Problem

The Windows `Electron Tests` job in build [438755](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=438755) failed on attempt #1 even though all tests passed. The only failing step was the 1ES auto-injected **Publish Log Files** output:

```
System.IO.IOException: The process cannot access the file
'D:\a\_work\1\s\.build\logs\smoke-tests-electron\16_suite_Task\main.log'
because it is being used by another process.
```

Same lock affected `ptyhost.log`, `network-shared.log`, `mcpGateway.log`, `sharedprocess.log`, `tunnelHostService.log`, `userDataSync.log` — all from the `Task` smoke suite.

## Root cause

On Windows, when the Electron main process exits, its utility processes (ptyHost, sharedProcess, network-shared, GPU, renderers) can outlive it briefly and keep log files open. The existing `Diagnostics after smoke test run` step (which runs `tasklist /V`) confirmed this — at `02:03:10`, one second after smoke tests finished, **six** `Code - Insiders.exe` processes were still alive from `\test\VSCode-win32-<arch>\`. They were still around ~2 minutes later when `Publish Log Files` ran and tried to hash the locked files.

The smoke-test runner's `code.exit()` only polls the main PID and uses plain `process.kill(pid)` (no tree-kill), so child processes are not guaranteed to be reaped on Windows.

## Fix

Add a defensive cleanup step right after `Publish Tests Results` (the last user-controllable step before 1ES auto-injected `Publish Log Files`) that force-kills any process whose `ExecutablePath` is under `$(agent.builddirectory)\test\`.

- Path-scoped — can only target test artifacts (Electron + remote server binaries copied into the test dir), never system processes or the agent worker.
- `continueOnError: true` + `condition: succeededOrFailed()` — never blocks the build.
- Runs after Copilot extension tests so it doesn't interfere with running test phases.
- ~30 1ES auto-injected SDL/Guardian tasks run between this step and `Publish Log Files`, giving the OS plenty of time to fully release file handles.

title: fix: correct off-by-one in PreferredExtensionsPagedModel page lookup (fixes #316033)
body:
## 🔧 Error Fix

### Summary

**Error**: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'promise')` in `PreferredExtensionsPagedModel.resolve()`

**Root Cause**: Off-by-one error when indexing into `this.pages` array. The `pages` array has `totalPages - 1` entries because page 0 is pre-resolved via `firstPage` in the constructor. However, `resolve()` accesses `this.pages[pageIndex]` using the absolute 0-based page index from the pager. For pageIndex=1 (second page), this accesses `pages[1]` instead of `pages[0]`, and for the last page it accesses an out-of-bounds index, returning `undefined`.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#316033
Recommended reviewer: `@sandy081`

### Culprit Commit

The bug was introduced in [`1fd26136`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/1fd26136285b60269c2376b539fd9cbb67d7edfb) ("Implement infinite scrolling") by `@sandy081`, which added the `PreferredExtensionsPagedModel` class.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["paging.ts: DelayedPagedModel.resolve()"] --> B["extensionsViews.ts: PreferredExtensionsPagedModel.resolve()"]
    B --> C["this.pages[pageIndex] — OFF BY ONE"]
    C --> D["undefined.promise → TypeError"]
```

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsViews.ts` — `PreferredExtensionsPagedModel.resolve()`

### Repro Steps

1. Open Extensions view with a query that returns preferred extensions plus multiple pages of results
2. Scroll past the first page of results to trigger lazy page loading
3. `resolve()` computes `pageIndex >= 1` and accesses `this.pages[pageIndex]` which is off-by-one

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsViews.ts`): Changed `this.pages[pageIndex]` to `this.pages[pageIndex - 1]` to account for the fact that the `pages` array skips page 0 (which is pre-resolved via `firstPage` in the constructor). This fixes the data at its source — the incorrect array index mapping — rather than adding a guard at the crash site.

### Recommended Owner

`@sandy081` — author of the `PreferredExtensionsPagedModel` class and the infinite scrolling implementation.

title: Freeze customizations-index per conversation to stabilize system prompt cache
body:
Fixes #315408
Fixes #316182

## Why

The `<instructions>` / `<skills>` / `<agents>` listing rendered into the system prompt is recomputed on every turn from the live customizations index. Two unrelated sources of per-turn churn invalidate the system-level prompt cache breakpoint:

- **#316182** — switching modes mid-conversation rewrites which subagent is listed in `<agents>` (e.g. `Plan` ↔ `Ask`), changing a single line ~9.7k tokens into the system block.
- **#315408** — async-resolved experimentation/`setContext` flips a `when`-gated skill (e.g. `chronicle`) in or out of `<skills>` on later turns.

Either one trips the breakpoint and forces the model to re-cache the full system prefix every turn.

## What

Adds an experimental, default-off setting `github.copilot.chat.freezeCustomizationsIndex` (advanced / experimental / `onExp`, `ConfigType.ExperimentBased`). When enabled:

1. The first turn of a conversation snapshots the rendered customizations-index value + its tool references onto the `Turn` as `CustomizationsIndexMetadata`, keyed by the global-context cache key (workspace folders).
2. Every later turn reuses that frozen snapshot in the system prompt via `customizationsIndexOverride` on `<CustomInstructions>`, so the system prefix stays byte-identical.
3. If the live listing drifts from the snapshot, the updated set is appended to the *latest* user message inside `AgentUserMessage`'s `<Tag name='context'>` block as a `<customizationsUpdate>` tag. This lives inside the same `UserMessage` so it is captured by `RenderedUserMessageMetadata` and replays byte-identically on subsequent turns — no history poisoning.
4. Drift also fires with an empty value when the live variable disappears, so the model sees a clear "these are gone" signal rather than the stale frozen listing alone.

title: Fix Changes view stuck empty after first message in new agent host session
body:
## Fix

In the agents/sessions code, the "New Session" picker (`NewSession.session` in `baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts`) and the `AgentHostSessionAdapter` that the AHP server eventually creates for the same chat URI are two distinct `ISession` instances that share the same `sessionId`. The skeleton's UUID is intentionally reused as the committed session's URI path so the chat URI stays stable across the swap and the chat widget doesn't have to be re-opened against a different URI.

When `sendAndCreateChat` fired `_onDidReplaceSession({from: skeleton, to: adapter})`, `SessionsManagementService.setActiveSession(adapter)` hit this early-return:

```ts
if (previousSession?.sessionId === session?.sessionId) return;
```

…and silently skipped the swap. The active session kept holding the spread-copy of the skeleton, whose `changes` observable is a separate instance from the adapter's, so diffs that landed in the adapter (`AgentHostSessionAdapter.changes`) never reached subscribers — notably the Changes view, which stayed empty after the first message.

Switching to a different session and back was the only workaround, because the intermediate session has a different `sessionId`, breaking the early-return both times.

This change tracks the underlying `ISession` instance alongside `_activeSession` and requires **both** `sessionId` equality AND instance identity to early-return, so a same-id replace actually rewires the active session to the new instance.

A more invasive follow-up would unify `NewSession` and `AgentHostSessionAdapter` so a single instance gets "promoted" instead of replaced, but this fix is contained to the management service and addresses the symptom.

## Validation

- Reproduced #315936 with a fresh new local agent host session and an "append a single line to README.md" message — Changes view stayed empty.
- Confirmed the trace matches the diagnosis: `_handleDiffsChanged` writes diffs into `cached.changes`, `sessionFileChangesEqual` returns `false`, `_onDidReplaceSession` fires with `from.sessionId === to.sessionId`, and `setActiveSession` early-returns.
- After the fix the active session is rewired on replace and the view derived re-evaluates against the adapter's `changes` observable.
- `npm run compile-check-ts-native` passes.
- Existing `SessionsManagementService` unit tests pass (`./scripts/test.sh --grep deduplicateSessions`).

title: run_in_terminal: promote sync command to background after idle silence
body:
Re-land of #315885 on a standalone branch for isolated eval testing.

### What this does

If a synchronous `run_in_terminal` call produces **no terminal output for N ms** (default 60s), a new `idleSilence` race candidate wins the foreground race and promotes the execution to background. The process is **never killed** — the model gets the terminal ID + output so far and can `get_terminal_output`, `send_to_terminal`, or `kill_terminal`.

### Changes (3 files)
- **`runInTerminalTool.ts`**: New `idleSilence` race candidate using `RunOnceScheduler` + `onData` listener. Refactors `_buildInputNeededSteeringText` from `mentionTimeout: boolean` to `hungHint: 'none' | 'timeout' | 'idleSilence'` discriminator with per-mode wording.
- **`terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.ts`**: New setting `chat.tools.terminal.idleSilenceTimeoutMs` (default 60000, 0 disables, experimental).
- **`runInTerminalTool.test.ts`**: 3 unit tests for steering text across all hint modes.

### Why this is safe
- Commands that produce output regularly (`npm install`, `cargo build`, etc.) reset the timer and never trip.
- The async path is unchanged — it already has `OutputMonitor` idle detection.
- Listener + scheduler owned by `raceCleanup` `DisposableStore` — disposed when any other race candidate wins.

title: fix: guard against null in doRemoveFromValueTree (fixes #316034)
body:
## 🔧 Error Fix

### Summary

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Error | `Cannot convert undefined or null to object` |
| Bucket | `4f6775e2-741c-0fb1-53c4-75b6bf1f6251` |
| Version | 1.119.0 |
| Hits / Users | 1394 / 827 |
| Platforms | Windows, Mac, Linux |

`Object.keys()` throws when passed `null` inside `doRemoveFromValueTree` because `typeof null === 'object'` passes the existing type guard. This was triggered after the `agentsWindow` configuration extension point landed, which can introduce `null` default values into the configuration value tree.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#316034
Recommended reviewer: `@sandy081`

### Culprit Commit

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Commit | [`be340b1`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/be340b1fa87aac1afcf1ab501ee5cb86473c67a7) |
| Author | `@sandy081` |
| Date | 2026-05-06 |
| Title | Introduce proposed `agentsWindow` configuration extension point |

This commit introduced new configuration properties with `agentsWindow` defaults. When an extension is removed/updated, `updateConfigurationModel` calls `removeValue` for properties no longer in the registry. If any intermediate node in the value tree is `null`, the latent bug in `doRemoveFromValueTree` is triggered.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[configurationExtensionPoint._handler] -->|deltaConfiguration| B[configurationRegistry.deltaConfiguration]
    B -->|fires onDidUpdateConfiguration| C[DefaultConfiguration.onDidUpdateConfiguration]
    C --> D[updateConfigurationModel]
    D -->|property removed| E[ConfigurationModel.removeValue]
    E --> F[removeFromValueTree]
    F --> G[doRemoveFromValueTree]
    G -->|typeof null === 'object' passes guard| H[Object.keys null]
    H -->|CRASH| I[Cannot convert undefined or null to object]
```

### Affected Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/vs/platform/configuration/common/configuration.ts` | Contains `doRemoveFromValueTree` with the missing null guard |
| `src/vs/platform/configuration/common/configurationModels.ts` | `removeValue` calls `removeFromValueTree` |
| `src/vs/platform/configuration/common/configurations.ts` | `updateConfigurationModel` triggers removal |

### Repro Steps

1. Install an extension that contributes configuration properties with `null` default values (or values that resolve to `null` in the tree)
2. Update or uninstall the extension so its configuration properties are removed
3. `updateConfigurationModel` iterates removed properties and calls `removeValue`
4. `doRemoveFromValueTree` encounters a `null` intermediate node, `typeof null === 'object'` is `true`, and `Object.keys(null)` throws

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`src/vs/platform/configuration/common/configuration.ts:305`):

Added `value !== null` to the guard condition in `doRemoveFromValueTree`. The existing check `typeof value === 'object'` incorrectly allows `null` through because `typeof null === 'object'` is a well-known JavaScript quirk. By adding the explicit null check, we prevent `Object.keys(null)` from being called. This fixes the bug at the guard that produces invalid data flow (the data-producer principle) rather than wrapping downstream code in try/catch.

The fix is a single-character-level change to the condition: `typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)`. This is a standard JavaScript pattern for checking plain objects.

### Recommended Owner

`@sandy081` — author of the culprit commit and owner of the configuration infrastructure.

title: Terminal output compression: argv-aware filters, dedup cache, structured-data guard
body:
Fixes #315881

Follow-up to #315376 expanding terminal tool output compression.

### What's new

**Argv-aware command parsing** ([`terminalCommandParser.ts`](src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/terminalCommandParser.ts))
- POSIX-ish tokenizer (single/double quotes, backslash escapes).
- Composition splitter for pipelines and `&&` / `||` / `;` / `|&`, honoring quotes — `echo "a;b" | wc -l` correctly splits to 2 segments.
- Strips leading env assignments (`FOO=bar git diff`) and wrapper programs (`sudo`, `time`, `timeout`, `env`, `nice`, `xargs`, `unbuffer`, …).
- Filters now match on **any segment** of a pipeline, not just the head.

**12 filters** — git diff/show, git log, git status, ls (`-l` only), find/grep/tree (cap at 200 lines + summary), test runners (pytest/jest/vitest/cargo test/go test/npm test/npx X), build tools (cargo build/check/clippy, go build, make, tsc, gradle, mvn, dotnet build), linters (eslint/ruff/mypy/prettier/rubocop/golangci-lint/cargo clippy), npm install (audit/funding noise), env/printenv (sort + dedupe).

**Session-memory dedup cache** ([`terminalOutputCache.ts`](src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/terminalOutputCache.ts))
- Three TTL classes: Fast (30s, e.g. `git status`), Medium (120s), Slow (300s, e.g. `git log`).
- Mutation invalidation: `git commit` / `git checkout` clears `git status` / `git diff` entries in the same cwd.
- LRU-capped at 256 entries, keyed by `${cwd}::${command.trim()}`.
- `invalidateCwd()` external hook for editor file-write notifications.

**Registry-level guards** ([`toolResultCompressor.ts`](src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/tools/toolResultCompressor.ts))
- New `isProtectedFromCompression` skips JSON / YAML (`---\n`) / TOML (`[section]\n`) outputs even if a filter says it matches — never make structured data worse.
- New `cacheHit: boolean` field on the `toolResultCompressed` telemetry event.

### Acceptance criterion regression test
`gitDiffFilter` does NOT match `git difftool` (or `git diff-tree` / `git diff-files`) — only `git diff` and `git show`.

### Tests
- 76 new unit tests across `terminalCommandParser.test.ts`, `terminalOutputCache.test.ts`, and additions to `terminalOutputCompressor.test.ts`.
- 284 tests pass across the touched suites with 0 failures.
- `npm run compile-check-ts-native` clean.

title: fix: treat 'Failed to fetch' TypeError as OfflineError (fixes #315095)
body:
### Summary

`TypeError: Failed to fetch` is thrown by the browser's `fetch()` API when a network request cannot reach the server (DNS failure, no connectivity, captive portal, firewall block). Previously, `requestImpl.ts` only converted this to an `OfflineError` when `navigator.onLine` reported `false`. However, `navigator.onLine` is notoriously unreliable — it can report `true` during captive portals, intermittent connectivity loss, and DNS failures. When this happened, the raw `TypeError: Failed to fetch` propagated through `getAsset` → `getManifest` → `installFromGallery` → `doInstall` and reached error telemetry as an unhandled error.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#315095
Recommended reviewer: `@bpasero`

### Culprit Commit

No single culprit commit — this is a long-standing gap in the `requestImpl.ts` error handling. The `OfflineError` conversion was added for the `navigator.onLine === false` case but never extended to cover the case where `navigator.onLine` is unreliable.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[fetch API throws TypeError: Failed to fetch] --> B[requestImpl.ts catch block]
    B --> C{navigator.onLine === false?}
    C -->|Yes| D[throw OfflineError - handled gracefully]
    C -->|No| E[throw raw TypeError - reaches telemetry as unhandled]
    E --> F[getAsset fallback at extensionGalleryService.ts:1940]
    F --> G[getManifest at extensionGalleryService.ts:1779]
    G --> H[installFromGallery at extensionManagementService.ts:513]
    H --> I[doInstall at extensionsWorkbenchService.ts:2952]
    I --> J[unhandlederror telemetry]
```

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/base/parts/request/common/requestImpl.ts` — the `fetch()` error handler that produces the unhandled error

### Repro Steps

1. Open VS Code with unreliable network (captive portal or intermittent DNS failure where `navigator.onLine` still reports `true`)
2. Trigger extension installation from the marketplace
3. Both CDN and fallback requests fail with `TypeError: Failed to fetch`
4. Error reaches telemetry as `unhandlederror-Failed to fetch`

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`src/vs/base/parts/request/common/requestImpl.ts`):

Added a check after the existing `AbortError` and `TimeoutError` handlers: when the caught error is a `TypeError` with message `"Failed to fetch"`, throw `OfflineError` instead of re-throwing the raw error. This fixes at the data producer — the point where the browser's network error enters VS Code's error handling system — rather than at any downstream crash site. The `TypeError: Failed to fetch` message is the standard browser signal for network-level fetch failures, so reclassifying it as `OfflineError` is semantically correct. Downstream code (e.g., `extensionGalleryService.ts` lines 1483 and 1626) already handles `OfflineError` gracefully.

**Alternatives considered**:
- Wrapping the fallback request in `getAsset` with try/catch — this would silence the error at a consumer site rather than fixing the classification at the source.
- Adding `isOfflineError` checks in `installFromGallery` — same issue, guards at the crash site rather than fixing the producer.

title: sessions: use delegation for active session and force replace on session swap
body:
## Summary

Two improvements to `SessionsManagementService`:

### 1. Replace spread with `ActiveSession` delegation class

The active session was previously built by spreading an `ISession` into a new object (`{ ...session, activeChat }`). This creates a shallow copy that becomes stale — any properties that are later updated on the original session won't be reflected on the active session.

The new `ActiveSession` class implements `IActiveSession` by delegating all `ISession` property accesses to the underlying session via getters, keeping the active session always in sync with the live session state.

### 2. Force replace active session on `onDidReplaceSession`

When a session is replaced (e.g. a pending session transitions to a real one), `setActiveSession` was skipped if the session ID remained the same due to the early-return equality check. Now `onDidReplaceSession` passes `force: true` to bypass the check and fully rebuild the active session tracking (disposables, autoruns, context keys).

title: agentHost/claude: Phase 9 — abort + steering + changeModel + crash recovery
body:
Implements the runtime mutation surface for live Claude sessions.

## What

- **`abortSession`** — cancel via `_abortController.abort()` (mirrors production reference).
- **`setPendingMessages` steering** — `priority:'now'` `SDKUserMessage` injected into the live prompt iterable; `steering_consumed` signal fires on yield.
- **`changeModel` hot-swap** — `Query.setModel` + `Query.applyFlagSettings({ effortLevel })`. Runtime `'max'` → `'xhigh'` clamp at a single seam in `claudeModelConfig`.
- **Yield-restart primitive** — `ClaudeMaterializer` learns `'fresh' | 'resume'` start modes and a sibling `materializeResume()` that does NOT re-fire `onDidMaterializeSession`.
- **Subprocess-crash recovery** — `_fatalError` permanent-latch removed. `_rebindQuery('recover')` rebuilds the SDK plumbing on the next `send()` and replays bijective state (model + effort + permissionMode).

## Refactor

The old `claudeAgentSession` is split into three focused units, each with standalone unit test coverage:

| Class | File | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `ClaudePromptQueue` | `claudePromptQueue.ts` | 13 |
| `ClaudeSdkMessageRouter` | `claudeSdkMessageRouter.ts` | 5 |
| `ClaudeSdkPipeline` | `claudeSdkPipeline.ts` | 10 |

The pipeline tests intentionally cover only the synchronous lifecycle surface (abort / dispose / rebind / rematerializer wiring); the SDK message-stream end-to-end behavior is covered by `claudeAgent.test.ts`.

## Tests

- 28 new standalone unit tests for the three extracted classes.
- 10 new Phase 9 integration tests in `claudeAgent.test.ts`: abort/resend, steering preempt, `steering_consumed` echo, `changeModel` provisional + materialized + `'max'` clamp + id-only paths, crash recovery via resume, bijective state survival across restart.
- Full `agentHost` suite: **1519 passing**.
- `compile-check-ts-native` and `valid-layers-check` clean.

## E2E

Live operator scenarios A–D from `smoke.md` verified 2026-05-13: abort + resend, steering preemption + consumed signal, `changeModel` hot-swap mid-conversation, and the `'max'` → `'xhigh'` clamp warning.

## See

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/phase9-plan.md` — full contract, decisions, deviations, risks.
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/roadmap.md` — Phase 9 marked done.

title: Batch async terminal completion notifications
body:
Fixes #308932

When multiple async terminals complete around the same time (e.g. 5 parallel `npm install` commands), their steering notifications were being sent one at a time, creating 5 separate agent turns. Now they're debounced with a 500ms window per chat session and flushed as a single combined steering message.

### How it works
- `_enqueueCompletionNotification()` buffers completions per session with a `RunOnceScheduler`
- After 500ms of no new completions, `_flushCompletionBatch()` sends one combined message
- Single completions retain the existing format (no behavioral change)
- Batched completions use a summary format:
  ```
  [Terminal notification: 3 commands completed. Use send_to_terminal to send another command or kill_terminal to stop it.]
  - Terminal t1 (`npm install`) (exit code 0)
  - Terminal t2 (`npm test`) (exit code 1)
  - Terminal t3 (`npm build`) (exit code 0)

  Terminal t1 output:
  ...

  Terminal t2 output:
  ...
  ```

### Cleanup
- Pending batches are cancelled when chat sessions are disposed
- Scheduler is disposed after each flush

title: Suppress terminal-exited notifications during shutdown
body:
Fixes #314791

When VS Code shuts down, background terminals are disposed as part of normal cleanup. This triggers `terminal exited` system notifications via the `onDisposed` handler in `_registerCompletionNotification`. These notifications persist as undeliverable steering messages after restart, cluttering the chat UI and causing the agent to loop.

### Fix
- Inject `ILifecycleService` into `RunInTerminalTool`
- Set `_isShuttingDown = true` on `onWillShutdown`
- Skip the `terminal exited` steering message when the flag is set

This follows the same pattern used elsewhere in the terminal codebase (e.g. `terminalService.ts`, `decorationAddon.ts`).
